title: Council approves 2024 Regional budget and tax levy
subtitle: Also covered: homelessness funding, industrial land reserve, transit advertising, ION terminal location, acting CAO appointment, respiratory season update.
overview: Regional Council approved the 2024 operating budget, with a net expenditure of $1,510,130,581 and a property tax levy of $746,230,093, along with the capital budget and nine-year forecast {{vote:m13}}. The budget committee's recommendations included a one-time increase in food bank funding, money for the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness, a new youth fund, a bag tag fee increase to $3 from April 1, and a 10% cut to several discretionary grant envelopes. The transit cash fare increase was removed from the new fees by-law.

Council also created an Industrial Land Readiness Reserve, raised the limits on fully wrapped Grand River Transit buses, and endorsed a south terminal location for ION Stage 2. It approved a $1,000,000 annual Community Capacity Building Fund {{vote:m9}}, and authorized 2024 temporary borrowing {{vote:m12}}.

After a closed session, Council appointed Mathieu Goetzke as Acting Chief Administrative Officer {{vote:m14}}. The Medical Officer of Health reported that COVID-19, influenza and RSV continue to circulate and urged vaccination. Two long-serving staff members were thanked on their last day.

decisions.detail: Council approved the 2024 Plan, an operating budget with a $746,230,093 property tax levy, and the capital budget and forecast, as amended by Budget Committee.

The recommendations included $10.2 million toward the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness, a one-time food bank grant increase to $1.5 million, $150,000 a year for youth initiatives, and a $236,390 grant for A Better Tent City.
The bag tag fee rises to $3 from April 1, 2024, discretionary grant envelopes drop 10%, and the new fees by-law drops the transit cash fare increase.
Council established the reserve, with staff to recommend an initial $5 million transfer from other reserves and complete the strategy by the end of Q2 2024.

Council authorized Memoranda of Understanding with the Grand River Conservation Authority, approved a tax increment grant for 201 and 217 Hespeler Road in Cambridge, and endorsed location T1 for the ION Stage 2 south terminal.
Council directed staff to include $1,000,000 in the 2024 budget for an annual fund for priority-community organizations, with terms of reference due in Q1 2024.
Council approved the recommended priority project under P2023-30 and authorized staff to execute the funding agreements.
Mathieu Goetzke was appointed Acting CAO during the absence of the Chief Administrative Officer.

debate: Debate in the recorded portion was limited, since the budget deliberations took place earlier in the day at the Strategic Planning and Budget Committee.

On the Community Capacity Building Fund, one councillor asked why it had not been part of the budget process. Staff explained it was a November committee recommendation, and that a motion passed earlier in the day already covers the funding. Staff confirmed no additional $1,000,000 was being added.

The Chair said this year's budget process went much more smoothly than last year's, and noted the final budget had unanimous support despite competing needs and financial pressures on both the Region and residents.

During the respiratory update, a councillor asked about RSV vaccines. The Medical Officer of Health said the vaccine is not publicly funded and can be bought privately with a prescription from a primary care provider.
